advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a null `parent` (`_dispatch_payload(parent=None)`) is dropped rather than sent to Jira as `None`.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:125 — `for name, wrapper in (("priority", "name"), ("assignee", "name"), ("parent", "key")):` — parent now shares the `elif not value: del fields[name]` branch at :131-138
test at :294 exercises only `_dispatch_payload(assignee=None, priority=None)`; :296-298 assert only `"assignee" not in sent` and `"priority" not in sent`
parent tests (:301, :318) cover only truthy-string wrap and already-object passthrough; ABSENCE: no assertion on `parent=None` being dropped
advisory.finding: The newly-added `parent` field is wired into the shared falsy-drop branch (`elif not value: del fields[name]`) alongside assignee/priority, but no test exercises a null `parent`. The null-drop test only passes `assignee=None, priority=None`, so a regression that let a null parent reach Jira as `None` (the exact '400 data was not an object' class this diff fixes for assignee) would not be caught.
scenarios: The differ emits a `parent` key carrying `None` for a ticket with no parent, exactly as it does for assignee; a future refactor moves parent out of the drop loop or short-circuits it, and the null parent reaches Jira, 400ing the create — undetected by the suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend `test_a_null_valued_optional_is_dropped_rather_than_sent_as_null` (or add a sibling) to pass `parent=None` and assert `"parent" not in sent`.
